claims: The Go Blue Guarantee is a University of Michigan program providing free or reduced tuition for up to four years to in-state, full-time undergraduate students with a family income of $125,000 or less and assets below $125,000.
The Go Blue Guarantee applies to the Ann Arbor, Dearborn, and Flint campuses.
The Go Blue Guarantee covers tuition and mandatory fees for qualified students.
Go Blue Guarantee eligibility requires being a Michigan resident.
Go Blue Guarantee eligibility requires being a first-time bachelor's degree seeker.
Go Blue Guarantee eligibility requires enrolled full-time.
Students must submit the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) and the CSS Profile to be considered for the Go Blue Guarantee, per the U-M Financial Aid office.
The Go Blue Guarantee covers full tuition and mandatory fees for families with income ≤$125,000.
"Go Blue" originated in the 1950s (or possibly late 1940s) as a rallying cry, according to The University Record.
Various accounts attribute the popularization of "Go Blue" to student fans at hockey and football games, according to The University Record.
"Go Blue" is the primary slogan for U-M athletics.
The Go Blue App is a university AI assistant for student resources, dining, and campus life.
Go Blue, Go Abroad is a workshop and scholarship for first-year students to study abroad.
Go Blue Health is a cancer screening initiative by Northwell Health.
